item.research_question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to identify lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys in the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti system that maintain structural stability and high strength at elevated temperatures?
item.material_system: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 identified as successful LWHEAs)
item.processing_route: High-throughput CALPHAD-based computational screening (3246 alloys calculated with 5 at.% step size) followed by arc-melting of eight selected alloys with 99.9 wt% purity elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, and drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific samples.
item.test_conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 700 °C (strain rate 2 × 10−4 s−1); in situ neutron diffraction during uniaxial compression; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD; TEM and APT characterizations.
key_findings: Eight alloys were identified from 3246 initial compositions meeting criteria for Tm > 1250 °C and specific L21 phase fractions (0.05–0.5) at 0.5Tm and 0.8Tm.
Alloy 1 (Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5) exhibited a yield strength of 1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C and 607 ± 22 MPa at 700 °C.
Alloy 1 contained high-density nanoscaled L21 precipitates (10–30 nm) with a number density of 2.76 × 10^22/m^3 and volume fraction of 43.6 vol.%.
Alloys 2–7 formed ordered L21 antiphase domains (APDs) with ~85 vol.% fraction, behaving like a single L21 phase rather than a precipitation-strengthened composite.
The ordering transition temperature (Tc) for Alloy 1 was calculated at 1607 °C, significantly lower than Alloy 7's Tc of 1997 °C.
Precipitation strengthening in Alloy 1 contributed ~904 MPa to the yield strength, attributed to ordering strengthening.
Alloy 1 showed clear load-transfer behavior in neutron diffraction, whereas Alloy 7 showed synchronized lattice strain response indicating single-phase behavior.
item.mechanism: The formation of nanoscale L21 precipitates versus antiphase domains is governed by the deviation of chemical composition from the perfect L21 stoichiometry (Fe2AlTi-type). Alloys with compositions deviating from stoichiometry (G1) form precipitates within a BCC matrix, enabling precipitation strengthening via load transfer. Alloys matching stoichiometry (G2) form a single-phase L21 structure with APDs. The order-disorder transition temperature is controlled by atomic-site occupancy and interaction energies (e.g., Fe–Al, Fe–Ti pairs favor L21; Cr–Fe pairs favor BCC), where lower Tc allows retention of the BCC matrix alongside L21 precipitates.
item.limitations: The current thermodynamic database requires improvement regarding the stability of the L21 phase, as evidenced by the microstructure discrepancy between prediction and observation for Alloys 2–7. The high-throughput predictions are currently valid only in the composition range of Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.% with unchanged contents of other elements.
item.future_work: Long-period annealing on the identified alloys and quantitative characterization are necessary to improve the thermodynamic database. The high-throughput design method should be coupled with the deciphered atomic occupancy rules to accelerate the discovery of advanced HEAs, particularly for multicomponent systems.
quotes: Through the high-throughput screening, precipitation-strengthened lightweight high-entropy alloys are discovered from thousands of initial compositions, which exhibit enhanced strengths compared to other counterparts at room and elevated temperatures.
The high-density nanoscaled L21 precipitates (10–30 nm) that are uniformly distributed within the BCC matrix are found in Alloy 1 (Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5) and Alloy 8 (Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5).

The ordering transition temperature, Tc, of Alloy 1 [1607 °C (1880 K)] is much lower than that of Alloy 7 [1997 °C (2270 K), far beyond its melting temperature], suggesting that the ordered L21 phase is less easily retained in the solid state in Alloy 1 than in Alloy 7.
